# Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta (MN 10 (PTS MN i 55))

**ID:** MN 10 (PTS MN i 55)  
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)  
**Collection:** Sutta  
**Title (Pali):** Mahāsatipaṭṭhāna Sutta  
**PTS:** MN i 55  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0201m.mul0.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0201m.mul0.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Satipaṭṭhānasutta* (MN 10) is the tenth discourse in the *Majjhimanikāya*, addressed to the monks and setting out the four establishments of mindfulness as the direct path to Nibbāna and the seventh factor of the noble eightfold path [Shonin et al. 2015; Anālayo 2003]. The sutta organizes meditative practice into four sequential domains: contemplation of the body (*kāya*), feelings (*vedanā*), mind (*citta*), and mind-objects or phenomena (*dhamma*) [Anālayo 2014; Wen]. Within body contemplation, it incorporates the first tetrad of mindfulness of breathing, awareness of the four bodily postures, bodily anatomical parts, and charnel ground reflections [Anālayo 2014; Anālayo 2019; Wen].

 Accompanied by its commentary, MN 10 has served as a foundational source for Theravāda meditation manuals and remains central to the 20th-century *vipassanā* revival and contemporary mindfulness practice [Crosby; Stanley et al. 2018; Walshe 1987].

**Sources**

- [Shonin et al. 2015] Edo Shonin, William Van Gordon, and Nirbhay N. Singh, eds., Buddhist Foundations of Mindfulness (2015) — Position of MN 10 in the Majjhima Nikāya, audience, and comparison of the four truths section with DN 22.

- [Stanley et al. 2018] Steven Stanley, Ronald E. Purser, and Nirbhay N. Singh, Handbook of Ethical Foundations of Mindfulness (2018) — Usage of MN 10 among contemporary mindfulness practitioners.
- [Walshe 1987] Maurice Walshe, The Long Discourses of the Buddha: A Translation of the Dīgha Nikāya (1987) — Verbatim correspondence between DN 22 and MN 10.
- [Anālayo 2019] Bhikkhu Anālayo, Mindfulness of Breathing: A Practice Guide and Translations (2019) — Analysis of the first tetrad of mindfulness of breathing in MN 10 and its parallels.
- [Anālayo 2014] Bhikkhu Anālayo, Perspectives on Satipaṭṭhāna (2014) — Modes of body contemplation and comparisons with MN 119 and Chinese Āgama parallels.
- [Anālayo 2003] Bhikkhu Anālayo, Satipaṭṭhāna: The Direct Path to Realization (2003) — Structure of MN 10 and comparison of the four noble truths exposition with DN 22.
- [Wen] Tzungkuen Wen, A Study of Sukkhavipassaka in Pāli Buddhism — Stock definition of satipaṭṭhāna, four postures, and the commentary's perspective on dry insight.
